character_sheet: A small, round forest animal with a blocky head, buck teeth and a broad flat tail. It waddles on four stubby feet in a brisk trot, chews constantly whether it is walking or not, and slowly rocks its tail. It is timid: it keeps away from monsters and from players, bolts in a panic when hurt, floats in water, and pairs up to breed (the baby is the same rig at half size). Its one job is wood: it looks for logs nearby and chews them down with a chainsaw sound. It never attacks. Read it as a busy, nervous little worker — quick feet, restless jaw, calm tail.
size_notes: Drawn at x0.75 of the rig (a 0.6 x 0.8 block hitbox); the baby form at x0.375. The tail is the widest part.

groups.name: gait
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.45 = 1.414 rad (81 deg) x limbSwingAmount
groups.plain: the four feet swing fore-and-aft as a trot: right-front with left-rear, left-front with right-rear (the opposite sign); the swing shrinks to nothing when the beaver stands still
groups.math: rff.xRot = lrf.xRot = cos(ageInTicks * 3.7) * pi * 0.45 * limbSwingAmount; lff.xRot = rrf.xRot = -(that)

groups.name: teeth
groups.plain: the teeth chew continuously, walking or standing

groups.name: tail
groups.plain: the flat tail rocks slowly up and down, one rock every 12.6 ticks (0.63 s)

behaviour: Three independent rhythms run at once: a fast trot on the feet (scaled by walking speed), a chew on the teeth and a slow tail rock; nothing else moves (the head and nose are static).
Standing still, the feet hang at the bind pose while the teeth and tail keep going: today's 'idle' is the walk at zero speed plus the free-running chew and rock (contract §2.1).
The head does not track the player: the classic model has no head-yaw channel.
The pose is code-driven in the shipped build (the harness reference leg); the artist clips replace it under the modern config once the contract is wired.
